We have demonstrated a novel optical method to detect defects in patterned 22-nm node wafers using quantitative phase and phase gradient images from epilumination diffraction phase imaging.
We demonstrated that epiillumination phase microscopy can achieve a diffraction-limited lateral resolution of 0.36 micrometers and that it can detect defects in 22 nm node wafers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel optical techniques for the inspection and characterization of semiconductor wafers.
the study of light propagation and imaging in complex optical systems.
the study of the optical response of nanostructured materials and nanostructures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of epiillumination in diffraction phase microscopy has enabled a 20 nm lateral resolution, which is the highest lateral resolution ever demonstrated in optical microscopy.

the use of the phase image is a powerful tool in defect inspection, and the combination of phase and amplitude images is a very powerful tool for defect inspection and characterization, especially for the 22 nm node and beyond.
the 22 nm node patterned wafer was free of defects, which was a major achievement for the 22 nm technology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can detect defects in a wafer that has a patterned feature size of 22 nm using only visible light and a standard microscope.
we can detect and localize 20 nm by110 nm defects on a 22 nm patterned wafer using a simple, low cost and easy to use optical microscope.
we are using the diffraction of visible light to find defects in a wafer with 22 nm node features.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diffraction limited resolution of visible light is not a limitation in detecting nanoscale defects in a 2D periodic pattern.
the diffraction limited lateral spatial resolution is sufficient for defect detection and characterization.
diffraction limited imaging can detect defects in the sub-50 nm range, even when the defects are buried in the bulk of a wafer, and that this is possible using visible light.
